method: Drive networks per district, projected to UTM before measurement. Counts are normalised by the district's projected area. Orientation bins are share of street length per 10° compass sector.
caveat: Street geometry is among the best-mapped data in OSM, but these figures describe what OSM contains rather than an official cadastre, and district boundaries are OSM's, not an administrative gazetteer's — mostly mapper-drawn place polygons rather than official limits. Downtown Cairo is the exception: OpenStreetMap has no polygon for it at all, under any name or tag, so its extent is drawn by hand from the district's known edges (the Nile, Ramses, Port Said Street, Sayyida Zeinab). Every district carries boundary_source saying which it is. Because per-km² figures depend on where the line falls, Downtown's density numbers are the ones most sensitive to that choice.

districts.name: Downtown Cairo
districts.why: Ismail's Paris-on-the-Nile: deliberate boulevards and midans laid over a dense grid. The oldest planned fabric in the comparison.

districts.name: Heliopolis
districts.why: Baron Empain's tram-served desert suburb — radial avenues over a regular grid, built around public transit from day one.

districts.name: Maadi
districts.why: Delta Land Company's low-density villa quarter: numbered streets on a grid, softened by diagonals and greenery.

districts.name: Nasr City
districts.why: The state's post-revolution answer to Cairo's growth — wide arterials and superblocks, designed for the car era.
